findings.title: limitFunction drops all caller arguments
findings.cause: The returned wrapper ignores its own arguments and always calls the original function with no parameters: `return () => limit(() => function_());`.
findings.impact: Every real use of `limitFunction(fn)` with parameterized calls receives `undefined` arguments. This breaks the documented reusable-function recipe and the generic TypeScript signature that promises `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`.
findings.evidence: index.js:121-125 implements a zero-argument wrapper. index.d.ts:133-136 declares that the returned function accepts the original function arguments. recipes.md:151-163 shows `fetchUrl(url)` wrapped with `limitFunction` and then called as `limitedFetchUrl(url)`. benchmark.js:193-194 calls `limitedTask(delay, i)`, which this implementation discards.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory runtime probe of index.js with a minimal Queue stub: `const limited = limitFunction(async (value, suffix) => `${value}:${suffix}`, {concurrency: 1}); await limited('A', 'B')` returned `undefined:undefined` instead of `A:B`.

findings.title: limit.map omits the index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The mapper call passes `undefined` as the index unless `Array.isArray(iterable)` is true.
findings.impact: `limit.map(new Set(...), mapper)` and iterator inputs no longer match the documented contract. Consumers using the index for correlation, output labels, or stable ordering logic get `undefined` for every non-array item.
findings.evidence: index.js:106-114 computes `iterableIsArray` and passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`. readme.md:78-85 says the mapper receives item value and index and is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))`. index.d.ts:40-43 types the mapper index as `number` for any `Iterable<Input>`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory runtime probe: `await limit.map(new Set(['x', 'y']), (value, index) => { seen.push([value, index]); return value; })` recorded `[['x', undefined], ['y', undefined]]`; JSON output showed `[["x",null],["y",null]]` because JSON stringifies `undefined` array slots as `null`.

findings.title: Options-object clearQueue rejects by default despite documented default false
findings.cause: Destructuring sets `rejectOnClear = true` whenever an options object is used.
findings.impact: Calling `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` changes `clearQueue()` from discarding pending work to rejecting pending promises with `AbortError`. That is a breaking behavior difference from the documented default and can unexpectedly fail `Promise.all` callers that only switched from numeric concurrency to an options object.
findings.evidence: index.js:6-8 sets `rejectOnClear = true` for options objects. readme.md:46-52 and readme.md:149-155 document `rejectOnClear` as boolean default `false`. index.d.ts:99-106 also documents default `false`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory runtime probe: with `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1})`, one running task and one queued task, `limit.clearQueue()` made the queued promise win a race as `rejected:AbortError`; the documented default would leave it pending/discarded unless `rejectOnClear: true` was explicitly supplied.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass runtime validation
findings.cause: The runtime check only validates `rejectOnClear` when the value is truthy: `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`.
findings.impact: Invalid option values such as an empty string, `0`, or `null` are silently accepted even though the public option is boolean. This creates inconsistent validation: truthy strings throw, while falsy non-booleans change behavior by disabling rejection.
findings.evidence: index.js:12-14 gates the type check on truthiness. readme.md:46-50 says `rejectOnClear` is boolean. index.d.ts:99-106 declares `readonly rejectOnClear?: boolean`, and index.test-d.ts:29 only covers the truthy string case `'nope'`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory runtime probe: `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: ''})` was accepted instead of throwing `TypeError`.
